recipes.name: Chile-Garlic Shrimp
ingredients_raw: 1 pound uncooked medium shrimp, peeled and deveined
1 (1.6 oz) package buffalo wing seasoning mix (such as McCormick® Original Buffalo Wings Seasoning Mix)

steps.text: Rinse the shrimp with cold water and pat dry with paper towls. Add the shrimp and seasoning mix to a plastic bag and shake to coat.

Heat the butter, garlic, and red pepper flakes in a large skillet over medium heat until the butter has melted. Raise the heat to medium-high; when the butter begins to pop and sizzle add the shrimp to the pan. Cook and stir the shrimp until they are bright pink on the outside and the meat is no longer transparent in the center, about 4 to 5 minutes. Do not overcook.
Remove the pan from the heat and stir in the cilantro and lime juice. Garnish with lime wedges and serve hot.

raw_recipe.headline: Chile-Garlic Shrimp
raw_recipe.description: Buffalo wing seasoning, garlic, cilantro, and lime are the secret ingredients in this simple shrimp dish.

review.reviewBody: These were really good and so easy to make! I will for sure them again. I also coulnt find the powder buffalo seasoning so I used about 1/2 cup of my favorite bottled buffalo sauce and put them in a baggie with it and shook them to spead it all over. Then followed the directions from there.I served them with rice.

Deliciously spicy! I made it as a meal with rice on the side and a simply dressed salad. I added a sprinkle of cotija cheese on top. My husband said it’s one of the best things I’ve ever made. I messed up by buying flat leaf parsley instead of cilantro….honest mistake. I’ll just have to make it again.
I didn't have any buffalo wing seasoning so I made up my own with taco seasoning and garlic jalapeño seasoning. It worked really well. Especially if you like spicy.

I used frozen, cooked shrimp (thawed and patted dry). I only had eight shrimp. I used butter, bottled buffalo sauce, dried chile flakes, a good pinch of brown sugar, and a couple pinches of cornstarch. Garlic would have been good, but I forgot it. I cooked it in a wok, and ate it on salad. Delicious. Very, very quick prep time. I will do this again and again.

As a chef I do not use commercial herb or spice mixes but I do make a buffalo wings mix and I used that. The recipe is possibly a good beer accompaniament but I prefer to taste the shrimp. Thia is the start of spot-prawn season here and all they need is to be alive and steamed like a lobster or a crab, in fresh chives, butter, fresh milled black pepper and white wine.

So simple and good! We’re not huge spicy people so I skipped the red pepper flakes and it was plenty spicy for us. I couldn’t find the buffalo chicken mix so I ordered it on Amazon. Glad it was good because I had to buy six packages there. The only other change I may try next time is fresh garlic instead of the bottled minced stuff. I just served it with rice and it was a simple tasty dinner. Will add this to our regular rotation.
This is definitely a keeper. Easy to make and just delicious! I only had cooked shrimp so I let them cooked for about 3 minutes. The lime and the cilantro at the end make it outstanding.
Wasn't sure what else to have with the shrimp, so we added some peppers and onions and turned them into fajitas.
It was amazing. Substituted 3 tablespoons of oil and 2 tablespoons of butter instead of 5 tablespoons butter for a more healthier approach. Still turned out amazing
I had to use Buffalo Sauce instead of seasoning mix, and dried cilantro instead of fresh cilantro, and the shrimp still turned out great. Easy and delicious!

Wonderful & easy!!! I detest peeling & deveining shrimp so use big cooked shrimp from the freezer. Thaw and add to sauce in the last 3 minutes to heat through. Everyone loves this as an appetizer or entree.
m? M?? M Mmm m? Mm? m mm m mm mommym
Made this recipe as is. Served as a lite dinner. Fantastic. Will definitely make again, and even serve as an appetizer. Love it!

SO SIMPLE AND DELICIOUS!

I made this recipe last night for my family and they loved it. It had just the right amount of heat and a great depth of flavor. Unfortunately, I only had salted butter so it was a little saltier than I like. So, follow the directions and use unsalted butter. When you toss it with the fresh lime juice and cilantro, you end up with shrimp that has a lot of depth of flavor. I'm definitely going to try this on my charcoal grill next summer. I think that it would even be good as an appetizer if you chill the shrimp after they are cooked and serve it with salsa and/or lime crema to dip the shrimp into

I made this following the recipe. My husband likes spice but I do not. However, this recipe was good and easy. I will make it again. I served it with gluten free rotini noodles, broccoli and a salad with ranch dressing. The ranch dressing on the salad allowed me to "cool" my bites, My husband loved it.
I used 1/4 cup buffalo sauce
It was great. I will be making this a lot as I am a shrimp fanatic.
Wow! Great recipe! However, I found that if you replace the cilantro with zucchini peels it tastes a lot better. It gives those shrimp an extra kick of flavour!
Food is Immaculate

10.31.21 Tender, succulent shrimp with a tangy sauce and a little kick of spiciness. What a nice recipe made with so little effort. Your cook time will depend on the size of the shrimp, just be sure not to overcook. I used garlic paste in a tube (Gourmet Garden®) instead of bottled minced garlic and served with Classic Fried Rice, another recipe from this site.
